SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / CABINS & PRIVACY

Transforming spaces with office cabin designs.

Plan for the work, not just the title on the door. This Space Craft planning note looks at transforming spaces with office cabin designs through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEList the activities insideBalance enclosure and connectionTest furniture as a settingMap activity before assigning desksBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

List the activities inside

An enclosed room may need to support focused work, confidential calls, short meetings and occasional presentations. Prioritise the actual mix before choosing the desk and storage.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Balance enclosure and connection

Position doors and glazing with attention to privacy and the wider office. Visual openness does not automatically provide speech privacy; review acoustic requirements separately.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Test furniture as a setting

Draw the desk chair in use, visitor seats pulled out and cupboard doors open. These checks expose conflicts that a neat furniture outline can hide.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Map activity before assigning desks

Write down the tasks people perform, how often teams overlap and when visitors arrive. A desk count alone will not reveal the need for private calls, project tables or storage.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Agree the real purpose and occupancy of the room.
  • Check speech privacy and glare on screens.
  • Test furniture access and daily movement.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.

General design considerations for discussion. Product suitability, technical performance, statutory requirements and project pricing need appropriate, project-specific review. Images are illustrative.
